Which statement about paper chromatography is correct?

options.text: A solvent is needed to dissolve the paper.
Paper chromatography separates mixtures of solvents.

questions.questionText:
Element X has 7 protons.
Element Y has 8 more protons than X.
Which statement about element Y is correct?

options.text: Y has more electron shells than X.
Y has more electrons in its outer shell than X.
Y is in a different group of the Periodic Table from X.
Y is in the same period of the Periodic Table as X.

questions.questionText:
A covalent molecule Q contains only six shared electrons.
What is Q?
Which statement explains why metals are malleable?

options.text: The atoms release electrons to become cations.
The electrons are free to move.
The electrons and the cations are attracted to each other.
The layers of ions can slide over each other.

questions.questionText: Which statement about isotopes of the same element is correct?

options.text: They have different numbers of electrons.
They have different numbers of neutrons.
They have different numbers of protons.
They have the same mass number.

questions.questionText:
The element silicon has the same structure as diamond.
Which statement about silicon is correct?

options.text: Every silicon atom is bonded to three other atoms only.
Silicon has a high melting point.
Silicon is a good conductor of electricity.
Silicon is used as a lubricant.

questions.questionText:
In separate experiments, electricity was passed through concentrated aqueous sodium chloride
and molten lead(II) bromide.
What would happen in both experiments?

options.text: A halogen would be formed at the anode.
A metal would be formed at the cathode.
Hydrogen would be formed at the anode.
Hydrogen would be formed at the cathode.

questions.questionText:
Gas syringe X contains 100cm3 of hydrogen bromide gas, HBr.
Gas syringe Y contains 100cm3 of carbon dioxide gas. The volume of each gas is measured at
room temperature and pressure.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The mass of HBr is less than the mass of CO .
The number of molecules of HBr equals the number of molecules of CO .
The gas in syringe X contains more atoms than the gas in syringe Y.
The number of moles of HBr is more than the number of moles of CO .

questions.questionText:
An example of a redox reaction is shown.
Zn + Cu2+  Zn2+ + Cu
Which statement about the reaction is correct?

options.text: Zn is the oxidising agent and it oxidises Cu2+.
Zn is the oxidising agent and it reduces Cu2+.
Zn is the reducing agent and it oxidises Cu2+.
Zn is the reducing agent and it reduces Cu2+.

Which row describes X and XO?
element X nature of oxide, XO

● Its atoms have four electrons in their outer shell.
● It is a non-metal.
● Its oxide has a macromolecular structure.

Which property is shown by transition elements?

Helium and neon exist as monoatomic gases at room temperature and pressure.
statement 1 Helium and neon have eight electrons in their outer shell.
statement 2 Helium and neon are unreactive.
Which option is correct?

options.text: Statement 1 is correct and explains statement 2.
Statement 1 is correct, but does not explain statement 2.
Statement 1 is incorrect, but statement 2 is correct.

questions.questionText: Which statement explains why galvanising prevents iron from rusting?

options.text: Zinc is more reactive than iron and corrodes in preference to iron.
Zinc is more reactive than iron and loses electrons less easily than iron.
Zinc is less reactive than iron and corrodes in preference to iron.
Zinc is less reactive than iron and loses electrons more easily than iron.

options.text: It is made by the thermal decomposition of limestone.
It is used to neutralise alkaline soils.
It is a reactant in the test for carbon dioxide.
